[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Big Data SQL: Spark SQL Tutorial"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark SQL is a Spark module for structured data processing. It provides a programming interface similar to traditional SQL, allowing you to query structured data inside Spark programs using either SQL or a familiar DataFrame API. Spark SQL supports a variety of data sources, including Hive, Parquet, JSON, and more."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of SQL."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Familiarity with Apache Spark concepts (RDDs, DataFrames)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A working Spark environment (local mode or cluster)."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Setting Up Spark SQL"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"First, ensure you have Spark installed and configured. You'll typically interact with Spark SQL through the `SparkSession` object, which is the entry point for Spark functionality."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

# Create a SparkSession
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("Spark SQL Example") \
    .getOrCreate()"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"This code snippet creates a `SparkSession` named 'Spark SQL Example'. If one already exists, it retrieves it; otherwise, it creates a new one."},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"Creating DataFrames"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark SQL primarily works with DataFrames, which are distributed collections of data organized into named columns. You can create DataFrames from various sources."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"From RDDs"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can create a DataFrame from an existing RDD. You'll need to define a schema for the data."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import Row

# Create an RDD
data = [Row(name='Alice', age=30), Row(name='Bob', age=25)]
rdd = spark.sparkContext.parallelize(data)

# Create a DataFrame
df = spark.createDataFrame(rdd)

df.show()"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example creates an RDD of `Row` objects and then converts it into a DataFrame. The `show()` method displays the DataFrame's contents."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"From Data Sources (CSV, JSON, Parquet)"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark SQL can read data directly from various file formats."},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"# Read a CSV file
df_csv = spark.read.csv("data.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)

# Read a JSON file
df_json = spark.read.json("data.json")

# Read a Parquet file
df_parquet = spark.read.parquet("data.parquet")

df_csv.show()
df_json.show()
df_parquet.show()"},{"order":20,"type":"paragraph","text":"The `inferSchema=True` option in `read.csv` attempts to automatically determine the data types of the columns.  Make sure your data is consistent for this to work correctly."},{"order":21,"type":"heading","text":"Querying Data with SQL"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark SQL allows you to execute SQL queries against DataFrames. First, you need to register the DataFrame as a temporary view."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"# Register the DataFrame as a temporary view
df_csv.createOrReplaceTempView("people")

# Execute a SQL query
results = spark.sql("SELECT name, age FROM people WHERE age > 25")

results.show()"},{"order":24,"type":"paragraph","text":"This code registers the `df_csv` DataFrame as a temporary view named 'people' and then executes a SQL query to select names and ages of people older than 25. The result is another DataFrame."},{"order":25,"type":"heading","text":"DataFrame API"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Besides SQL, you can also use the DataFrame API for data manipulation."},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Selecting Columns"},{"order":28,"type":"code","text":"# Select specific columns
df_names_ages = df_csv.select("name", "age")
df_names_ages.show()"},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"Filtering Rows"},{"order":30,"type":"code","text":"# Filter rows based on a condition
df_older_than_25 = df_csv.filter(df_csv["age"] > 25)
df_older_than_25.show()"},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"Grouping and Aggregating"},{"order":32,"type":"code","text":"from pyspark.sql import functions as F

# Group by a column and calculate the average age
df_avg_age = df_csv.groupBy("name").agg(F.avg("age").alias("average_age"))
df_avg_age.show()"},{"order":33,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example groups the DataFrame by 'name' and calculates the average age for each name using the `avg` function from `pyspark.sql.functions`. The `alias` function renames the resulting column."},{"order":34,"type":"heading","text":"Saving DataFrames"},{"order":35,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can save DataFrames to various file formats."},{"order":36,"type":"code","text":"# Save the DataFrame to a Parquet file
df_csv.write.parquet("output.parquet")

# Save the DataFrame to a CSV file
df_csv.write.csv("output.csv", header=True)"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"The `header=True` option in `write.csv` includes the column names in the output CSV file."},{"order":38,"type":"heading","text":"Working with Hive"},{"order":39,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark SQL can seamlessly interact with Hive, allowing you to query Hive tables directly."},{"order":40,"type":"code","text":"# Enable Hive support
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("Spark Hive Example") \
    .enableHiveSupport() \
    .getOrCreate()

# Execute a Hive query
results = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM my_hive_table")

results.show()"},{"order":41,"type":"paragraph","text":"The `enableHiveSupport()` option enables integration with Hive.  Ensure Hive is properly configured and accessible to your Spark environment."},{"order":42,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"Spark SQL provides a powerful and flexible way to process structured data at scale. Whether you prefer SQL or the DataFrame API, Spark SQL offers a unified interface for querying and manipulating data from various sources. This tutorial covered the basics of setting up Spark SQL, creating DataFrames, querying data, and saving results.  Further exploration of the Spark SQL documentation will reveal more advanced features and optimizations."}]
